video_title: Steady Lads Live From TOKEN2049 in Singapore (2026)
gist: Live Token2049 Singapore panel one year after the Oct-10 peak: panelists say everyone holds the same bags (HYPE, ZEC, Lighter, NEAR), debate Zcash as the coin of the cycle vs BTC (with $1K as the key level), Variational's Q4 TGE with a 32% airdrop, Pearl as a high-emission 'AI Bitcoin', and Tom Lee/BitMine flow trades. Consensus: the BTC bottom was in at $60K, but upside is selective and dispersion-driven.

themes.theme: Zcash as the coin of the cycle

insights.claim: A panelist who has been averaging up into Zcash and Hyperliquid calls Zcash the coin of the cycle and argues it has the best chance of competing with Bitcoin for flows, following the pattern where each cycle a new coin challenges an incumbent (ETH vs BTC, then Solana vs ETH).
insights.speaker: Zcash-holding panelist
insights.so_what: Frames ZEC as a rotation target away from BTC rather than a niche privacy coin.
insights.quote: I think Zcash has the biggest chance of competing for flows against Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Quantum risk is described as a major overhang on Bitcoin; contacts suggested BTC would trade around $120-150K if quantum were addressed, and Zcash's Project Tachyon upgrade (expected in coming months) plus the privacy narrative are cited as addressing it.
insights.speaker: Zcash-holding panelist
insights.so_what: Quantum-resistance progress is a catalyst for ZEC and a discount factor on BTC.

insights.claim: The Zcash bull defines $1,000 as the critical level: losing it would be bearish rather than a buy-the-retest opportunity, so his mental (not actual) stop loss is three-digit Zcash.
insights.speaker: Zcash-holding panelist
insights.so_what: $1,000 ZEC is the line the bulls themselves watch; a break could trigger capitulation.
insights.quote: So mentally my stop loss is three digit Zcash.

insights.claim: The Zcash bull targets $20-30K ZEC over the next couple of years but plans to start scaling out above $2K, around $3-4K.
insights.speaker: Zcash-holding panelist
insights.so_what: Gives explicit distribution levels for a crowded holder base.

insights.claim: Zcash was the worst-performing large asset over the prior seven days, and a host warned that reflexive assets like it bleed out once they stabilize because holders stop getting dopamine and drift away one by one.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Momentum-driven monetary assets are vulnerable to slow-bleed round trips after the run stalls.

insights.claim: Zcash has entered the top 10 with roughly $22 billion fully diluted value, alongside Hyperliquid, while Dogecoin is down about two-thirds and has not recovered, suggesting speculative alt flows have migrated to ZEC and HYPE.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Leadership rotated: the old speculative alts lost their bid to new favorites.

themes.theme: Crowded consensus bags and valuation risk

insights.claim: At Token2049 trading dinners, fund managers from Asia and the US all reported holding the same bags: Hyperliquid, Zcash, Lighter and NEAR.
insights.speaker: Zcash-holding panelist
insights.so_what: Positioning is extremely crowded in a handful of names, raising downside correlation risk.
insights.quote: I feel like everyone owns the same bag.

insights.claim: Valuations of buyback tokens like HYPE and Lighter have run so far that buybacks now have a tiny price impact because the market is pricing in roughly 100 years of revenue, raising concern about local highs.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Buyback narratives lose support power once multiples are this extended.
insights.quote: we're kind of pricing in 100 years of uh of like revenue at this point

insights.claim: The market has formed a barbell: pure cash-flow tokens (Hyperliquid-type) and pure monetary/memetic assets (Zcash, Pearl) are working, while mid-curve L1 tokens lag.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Avoid the middle: generic L1s lack both cash flow and monetary premium.

insights.claim: Justin (Variational head of product) sold 5-10% of his ETH near $4,850 and the rest after the October 10 crash at about $3,850, calling it the best decision of the cycle; ETH has since fallen to roughly $2,600-2,700 from about $4,400 a year earlier, and he recently exited Lighter at about $4.21.
insights.speaker: Justin
insights.so_what: A former ETH maxi fully exited ETH, an example of sentiment shift away from the asset.

themes.theme: Token launches and the corporate token dilemma

insights.claim: Variational plans its TGE in Q4 with roughly $4B+ daily volume and claims the largest airdrop in crypto history at 32% of supply, one point more than Hyperliquid's 31%.
insights.speaker: Justin
insights.so_what: The likely biggest TGE of the year continues the pattern of a major perp DEX token every Q4.

insights.claim: There have been essentially no new large token launches this year, not even a $1B TGE, and Q4 has repeatedly been when the cycle's big perp-DEX token launches (dYdX, Hyperliquid, Lighter, now Variational).
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Q4 perp DEX TGEs are a recurring seasonal setup traders can position for.

insights.claim: Public companies like Coinbase are unlikely to launch tokens because a token may hurt the equity, so the best strategy is to keep promising a Base token to drive activity, since farmers leave as soon as a token launches; private firms like Polymarket have more options, using a token as pseudo-equity to raise capital.
insights.speaker: Dim
insights.so_what: Treat Base token hints as a growth tactic, not an imminent catalyst.

insights.claim: Kraken's token is expected to launch within 3-6 months with a BNB-style utility vision as a wealth platform, but any fee-payment utility diverts cash flow from equity holders, creating an inherent conflict between token and equity.
insights.speaker: Host / Dim
insights.so_what: Exchange tokens with fee utility directly cannibalize equity cash flows.

insights.claim: Pearl, described as 'AI Bitcoin' that uses proof of useful work (AI inference compute) for mining, was the most frequently mentioned project in Korea and at trader dinners, yet trades only on an obscure KYC-free exchange with heavy friction, so a major listing could be a strong catalyst.
insights.speaker: Justin
insights.so_what: Access friction is the current edge; a listing is the catalyst.

insights.claim: A fund-side panelist warns Pearl emits roughly $1 million of inflation per day with supply doubling over the next year, so post-listing performance depends on demand exceeding sustained miner selling, making it very risky.
insights.speaker: Dim
insights.so_what: Heavy emissions are a structural overhang for any proof-of-work AI token.
insights.quote: I think supply is doubling over the next year.

insights.claim: People are starved for AI-economy assets; AI coins such as Grass (doubled since the previous episode), NEAR and Worldcoin are rallying, and the hosts expect strength to continue into an OpenAI IPO.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: An OpenAI IPO could be a sector-wide catalyst for AI tokens.

themes.theme: Tom Lee, BitMine and ETH flows

insights.claim: Tom Lee's BitMine is near its 5% ETH supply target, needing only a couple hundred million dollars more, and reportedly has about $400M in cash, with street rumors that he will kingmake ETH-ecosystem projects to boost ETH per share.
insights.speaker: Dim
insights.so_what: Once BitMine stops buying, ETH loses a major bid while ecosystem tokens may gain a backer.

insights.claim: As BitMine's ETH bid fades, a possible pair trade is long BitMine (or ETH ecosystem assets likely to get BitMine partnerships) versus short ETH.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: A specific relative-value idea built on treasury-company flow dynamics.

insights.claim: Tom Lee's strategy is framed as a left-curve version of Paradigm's last cycle: secure a large ETH bag, then work to support it (Paradigm by rewriting Ethereum client code and seeding Uniswap v4 liquidity), possibly more effectively since Paradigm appears to have given up.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Large holders defend their bags through ecosystem support, which shapes where flows go.

insights.claim: Kalshi's perpetuals volume appears to have been largely inorganic, with a few million of open interest against heavy wash trading, and Kalshi pulled out of a planned perps competition with Variational in Singapore.
insights.speaker: Justin
insights.so_what: Prediction markets moving into perps have not found real fit yet.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's HIP-3 is structurally a monopoly, but HIP-4 (prediction markets) has little traction because the UI does not suit prediction-market users, and the EVM and stablecoin efforts have not materialized; its success remains the core perp product.
insights.speaker: Dim
insights.so_what: New HIP initiatives are unlikely near-term drivers of a HYPE re-rating.

insights.claim: Options will be the next market that perp platforms compete over in Q1; order-book options on chain are hard, so Variational plans to bring its RFQ model to options and port TradFi liquidity on chain.
insights.speaker: Justin
insights.so_what: Watch for on-chain options launches from perp DEXs as the next competitive front.

insights.claim: Dim believes the bottom is in at $60K BTC and expects dispersion between a few strong assets and the rest; a sustained Bitcoin move requires the gold narrative to pick up, and he sees few cheap assets to re-enter now.
insights.speaker: Dim
insights.so_what: A BTC rally needs a gold-style narrative catalyst rather than broad beta.
insights.quote: I think we've put in the bottom at 60k

insights.claim: Justin is concerned that Bitcoin only fell about 50% (from about $110K to $60K) rather than the usual ~75%, so it may not have reset enough for an energetic bull run, and expects only an okay BTC performance.
insights.speaker: Justin
insights.so_what: A shallow drawdown may cap BTC upside this cycle.

insights.claim: Sentiment has flipped: the fear and greed index is around 70 versus 9-10 a few months ago, Robinhood bought $25M of BTC, and the market bottomed earlier than the four-year cycle implied, so speculation is back.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Corporate buying headlines and sentiment recovery signal a frothier phase.
insights.quote: I do feel like speculation is back on the menu.
